claims.text: Wear resistance of HEA coatings on transition-metal matrices initially increases as ambient temperature rises from 77 K to approximately 400–500 K.
The initial improvement in wear resistance is caused by deformation twinning and formation of a protective tribo-oxide layer.
Wear resistance degrades rapidly above approximately 500 K.
High-temperature degradation results from thermal instability of the oxide layer and a transition from TWIP to softening mechanisms.
CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA coatings can be deposited on a Q235 steel transition-metal matrix and evaluated under high-temperature friction and wear conditions.
The relevant HEA coating is single-phase or metastable FCC.
The relevant HEA coating has low stacking-fault energy.
Enhanced configurational entropy can stabilize single-phase high-entropy materials.
Low stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning in the HEA.
Deformation twinning enhances strain hardening and thereby improves wear resistance.
Frictional heating promotes formation of a protective oxide layer.
Sliding wear can produce chemical nanolayering associated with high wear resistance.
The sliding-induced chemical nanolayer in the proposed HEA system is a protective tribo-oxide film.
The critical stress for twinning in CrMnFeCoNi is approximately 235 ± 10 MPa.
As temperature rises, the resolved shear stress required for twinning decreases, allowing twinning to persist or shift.
Oxide layers can become unstable at a critical thickness and then crack or fracture.
Increasing ambient temperature beyond approximately 500 K reduces the thermodynamic stability of the protective oxide layer and causes cracking or spallation.
Elevated temperature may cause softening or a phase transition that reduces TWIP effectiveness and accelerates wear.
The predicted wear-rate curve has a minimum between approximately 400 K and 600 K and rises sharply above approximately 500 K.
Performance degrades if the resolved shear stress falls below the critical twinning stress, causing deformation to transition to dislocation slip or softening.
